full_list.title_en: Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
full_list.abstract: Molecular electronics offers a route toward continued device miniaturization, but reliable control of charge transport at the molecular scale requires a detailed understanding of the metal–molecule interface. In particular, the role of electrode geometry in determining transport behaviour remains less systematically explored than molecular structure and contact chemistry. Here, we investigate the influence of atomic-scale electrode geometry on the structural, electronic, quantum-transport, thermoelectric, and noise properties of Au–pentane–Au molecular junctions using a combined density functional theory–non-equilibrium Green's function (DFT–NEGF) and machine learning framework. Six representative electrode configurations—Flat Au(111), Pyramidal, Single Apex, Multi-Atom Tip, Nanowire, and Rough Surface—were structurally optimized and systematically compared while maintaining the same pentane molecular backbone and Au–S contact chemistry. The calculations reveal pronounced geometry-dependent variations in Au–S bonding, coordination number, contact area, molecular tilt, charge transfer, electronic-state alignment, and molecule–electrode coupling. These structural and electronic changes directly control quantum transport, with the calculated conductance decreasing from 0.92 G₀ for Flat Au(111) to 0.56 G₀ for the Single Apex configuration. Transmission, current–voltage characteristics, charge redistribution, and interface dipole analysis consistently demonstrate that highly coordinated and extended contacts provide stronger electronic coupling and more efficient transmission pathways. Thermoelectric calculations reveal an opposing trend: lower-coordination contacts exhibit enhanced Seebeck coefficients because of stronger energy dependence of transmission near the Fermi level, whereas the Flat Au(111) junction provides the highest calculated power factor and ZT ≈ 0.68. Shot noise, Fano factor, low-frequency noise, and Hooge-parameter analysis further demonstrate increasing transport fluctuations as electrode coordination decreases. To accelerate transport prediction, a dataset of 1500 configurations were constructed from structural and electronic descriptors extracted from the DFT–NEGF calculations. Among the tested models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance, with a testing R2 of 0.988, RMSE of 0.010 G₀, and MAE of 0.007 G₀. Feature-importance analysis identified Au–S bond length, HOMO–LUMO gap, coupling strength, DOS at the Fermi level, and Au 5d PDOS as the dominant predictors. The trained model successfully predicted conductance for previously unseen electrode configurations, demonstrating its potential for rapid screening of molecular junction structures.

full_list.title_en: High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
full_list.abstract: We present an accelerated materials discovery framework that combines diffusion-based crystal structure generation with hierarchical screening to identify new rare-earth–transition-metal magnets simultaneously achieving high magnetization and thermodynamic stability. Using this workflow, we systematically explored over 3000 binary (R-T) and ternary (R-T-T ′) compositions spanning R ∈ Y, Sm, T ∈ Fe, Co, Ni, and T ′ ∈ Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, and filtered approximately 240,000 generated crystal structures through machine-learning interatomic potential prescreening and spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) validation. We identify 300+ low-energy magnetic candidates within 0.1 eV/atom above the convex hull at the DFT level, including 5 thermodynamically stable phases. The highest saturation magnetization reaches ∼1.8 T in Fe-rich binary and ternary phases (SmFe 12 , YFe 12 , YFe 18 Ti and Sm 2 Fe 16 Mn). Symmetry analysis reveals that the majority of ternary candidates are subgroup derivatives of known binary prototypes through Wyckoff site splitting that accommodates T ′ substitution. Site-resolved magnetic moment analysis further shows that Mn aligns ferromagnetically with the Fe sublattice with minimal magnetization loss, whereas Cr couples antiferromagnetically, providing systematic guidance for dopant selection. These findings demonstrate a generalizable strategy for targeted magnetic materials discovery and suggest that extending generative searches to larger unit cells (>20 atoms) with higher Fe fractions is a promising route toward stable phases with saturation magnetization exceeding 1.8 T.

full_list.abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a process that occurs when the magnetic fields of a conductive plasma quickly rearrange and release massive amounts of stored magnetic energy. It is widely thought to be the underlying mechanism behind cosmic events such as solar flares and substorms in Earth's magnetosphere.

full_list.title_en: An extremely stable quantum gas offers a new lens on strongly interacting systems
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：An extremely stable quantum gas offers a new lens on strongly interacting systems
full_list.abstract: Molecular gases are a new form of artificial quantum matter. However, when these molecules collide, they are often lost extremely rapidly. Researchers from Radboud University and Columbia University have been able to suppress this collisional loss, paving the way for strongly interacting quantum matter. This new artificial quantum matter allows researchers to study quantum behavior relevant to electrons in real materials. Their results are published in Science.

full_list.abstract: Physicists at UC Santa Barbara have extended the search for evidence of microscopic black holes produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). The formation of these tiny, fleeting objects at the LHC represents one way theorists have sought to resolve anomalies in our understanding of the basic structure of spacetime, while the method used to look for them demonstrates a new way of searching for new particles.

full_list.title_en: Enhancing V2X Communication Security Using an MTCNN-LSTM-Based Multilevel Trust Evaluation Framework
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Enhancing V2X Communication Security Using an MTCNN-LSTM-Based Multilevel Trust Evaluation Framework
full_list.abstract: In the evolution of V2X infrastructure deployment, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication necessitates authentication, privacy, and dependability. Securing the V2X networks and charging issues is critical and more challenging due to the extensive infrastructure. This direction enables trust-based transactions between electric vehicles and the smart grid to fulfill energy consumption. This paper reveals the closed-loop V2X security and energy allocation system that integrates real-time multi-attack detection, dynamic trust evaluation, and battery optimization in an intelligent transportation system. In the proposed MTCNN-LSTM model, which incorporates multilevel trust and CNN-LSTM, we achieve 94.75% accuracy, 94.83% weighted F1-score, and 99.3% attack detection rate across four attack types (none, sybil, DDoS, and both). Trust based on nine telemetry features(security score, feedback score, behavior score, message frequency, message received, energy consumed, SoC, security score difference, energy consumed rate) It also optimizes the battery consumption during the attack, ensuring that the system can maintain functionality by detecting energy wastage based on the MTCNN-LSTM model, energy waste: 550 kWh at 30 % attack out of the supply by smart grid 2000 kWh for the given dataset "Electric Vehicle Trip Energy Consumption Data” in the simulation based on real data, class-weighted training and multi-speed validation to ensuring secure, resilient and sustainable energy in smart grid enabled V2X network.

full_list.title_en: The Darma Valley at the Himalayan Trijunction: Community, Territoriality, and Security Dynamics in the Borderland of India, China and Nepal
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：The Darma Valley at the Himalayan Trijunction: Community, Territoriality, and Security Dynamics in the Borderland of India, China and Nepal
full_list.abstract: Darma Valley is a high-altitude region in the Dharchula tehsil of Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, of the Rang or Darmiya Bhotiya community. Although small, the valley is structurally significant in the interface region along the borders of India, China, and Nepal, and it remains relatively understudied. Darma was one of only six passes officially designated for trade and pilgrimage under the Sino-Indian Agreement of 1954 between the Tibet Region of China and India. The centuries-old trans-Himalayan trading economy that sustained the valley became unviable after the Indo-Tibetan border was closed following the war of 1962, and the region was transformed into a heavily militarised border, guarded by the Indo-Tibetan Border Police. Based on the archival treaty material, colonial-era gazetteers, ethnographic scholarship, and government and news sources ranging from 1816 to 2026, this paper places the valley in the context of the larger frontier complex of Dharchula, located adjacent to the contested Trijunctions of Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhara, where multiple interpretations of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli continue to be a burden on India-Nepal relations with a certain studied ambiguity being displayed by China. In a borderland and securitisation approach the valley is explored as a miniature representation of the governance of the frontier in the Himalayas, where demographic retention, cultural continuity, pilgrimage tourism and infrastructure competition are as crucial in the definition of sovereignty as military presence, as shown in India's Vibrant Villages Programme or China's Xiaokang border village model. The analysis provides a geographically informed example of how human security and agency of the borderlands can be established in high-altitude border areas with contested claims.

core_items.title_en: Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
core_items.title_zh: 文献研究：Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
core_items.abstract: Molecular electronics offers a route toward continued device miniaturization, but reliable control of charge transport at the molecular scale requires a detailed understanding of the metal–molecule interface. In particular, the role of electrode geometry in determining transport behaviour remains less systematically explored than molecular structure and contact chemistry. Here, we investigate the influence of atomic-scale electrode geometry on the structural, electronic, quantum-transport, thermoelectric, and noise properties of Au–pentane–Au molecular junctions using a combined density functional theory–non-equilibrium Green's function (DFT–NEGF) and machine learning framework. Six representative electrode configurations—Flat Au(111), Pyramidal, Single Apex, Multi-Atom Tip, Nanowire, and Rough Surface—were structurally optimized and systematically compared while maintaining the same pentane molecular backbone and Au–S contact chemistry. The calculations reveal pronounced geometry-dependent variations in Au–S bonding, coordination number, contact area, molecular tilt, charge transfer, electronic-state alignment, and molecule–electrode coupling. These structural and electronic changes directly control quantum transport, with the calculated conductance decreasing from 0.92 G₀ for Flat Au(111) to 0.56 G₀ for the Single Apex configuration. Transmission, current–voltage characteristics, charge redistribution, and interface dipole analysis consistently demonstrate that highly coordinated and extended contacts provide stronger electronic coupling and more efficient transmission pathways. Thermoelectric calculations reveal an opposing trend: lower-coordination contacts exhibit enhanced Seebeck coefficients because of stronger energy dependence of transmission near the Fermi level, whereas the Flat Au(111) junction provides the highest calculated power factor and ZT ≈ 0.68. Shot noise, Fano factor, low-frequency noise, and Hooge-parameter analysis further demonstrate increasing transport fluctuations as electrode coordination decreases. To accelerate transport prediction, a dataset of 1500 configurations were constructed from structural and electronic descriptors extracted from the DFT–NEGF calculations. Among the tested models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance, with a testing R2 of 0.988, RMSE of 0.010 G₀, and MAE of 0.007 G₀. Feature-importance analysis identified Au–S bond length, HOMO–LUMO gap, coupling strength, DOS at the Fermi level, and Au 5d PDOS as the dominant predictors. The trained model successfully predicted conductance for previously unseen electrode configurations, demonstrating its potential for rapid screening of molecular junction structures.

core_items.title_en: High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
core_items.title_zh: 文献研究：High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
core_items.abstract: We present an accelerated materials discovery framework that combines diffusion-based crystal structure generation with hierarchical screening to identify new rare-earth–transition-metal magnets simultaneously achieving high magnetization and thermodynamic stability. Using this workflow, we systematically explored over 3000 binary (R-T) and ternary (R-T-T ′) compositions spanning R ∈ Y, Sm, T ∈ Fe, Co, Ni, and T ′ ∈ Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, and filtered approximately 240,000 generated crystal structures through machine-learning interatomic potential prescreening and spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) validation. We identify 300+ low-energy magnetic candidates within 0.1 eV/atom above the convex hull at the DFT level, including 5 thermodynamically stable phases. The highest saturation magnetization reaches ∼1.8 T in Fe-rich binary and ternary phases (SmFe 12 , YFe 12 , YFe 18 Ti and Sm 2 Fe 16 Mn). Symmetry analysis reveals that the majority of ternary candidates are subgroup derivatives of known binary prototypes through Wyckoff site splitting that accommodates T ′ substitution. Site-resolved magnetic moment analysis further shows that Mn aligns ferromagnetically with the Fe sublattice with minimal magnetization loss, whereas Cr couples antiferromagnetically, providing systematic guidance for dopant selection. These findings demonstrate a generalizable strategy for targeted magnetic materials discovery and suggest that extending generative searches to larger unit cells (>20 atoms) with higher Fe fractions is a promising route toward stable phases with saturation magnetization exceeding 1.8 T.

core_items.method_point: 方法上，这篇工作可归入磁性机器学习势、自旋 Hamiltonian、自旋—晶格动力学和非共线磁结构。从摘要能确认的线索包括：密度泛函理论和电子结构计算, 热力学自由能、相稳定与有限温度建模，以及铁电/多铁、极化翻转和电场驱动过程, 磁性、自旋以及自旋—晶格耦合对应的结构或物理量。若迁移到团队流程，应采用“训练集同时覆盖原子位移和自旋构型，显式标注交换、各向异性、DMI 或自旋力；用自旋 MD/MC 与 DFT 自旋能差验证温度、应变和缺陷下的磁序稳定性”的分层验证，而不是只比较单点能量或单一回归误差。还需核对原文的训练数据规模、损失函数、边界条件和误差分解，才能判断其是否适合团队的材料模拟任务。
core_items.related_work: 它与五位研究人员已有工作的直接连接是：磁性机器学习势、自旋 Hamiltonian、自旋—晶格动力学和非共线磁结构已经出现在团队的方向画像中，可对应到CrI₃/CrSBr 等范德华磁体、反铁磁/交替磁材料、磁性氧化物。与传统只做 0 K formation energy/静态势垒的工作相比，这里更应关注铁电/多铁、极化翻转和电场驱动过程, 磁性、自旋以及自旋—晶格耦合, 缺陷、畴壁、成核和开关动力学在温度、缺陷、应变或外场下的变化；摘要没有给出的模型细节不作延伸判断。这种联系应通过同一材料体系上的独立基准和跨分布测试确认，不能仅凭方法名称或期刊来源下结论。
core_items.implication: 对当前研究最具体的启示不是泛泛地“使用 ML”，而是把该文的磁性机器学习势、自旋 Hamiltonian、自旋—晶格动力学和非共线磁结构嵌入现有材料模拟链：先在CrI₃/CrSBr 等范德华磁体、反铁磁/交替磁材料、磁性氧化物中选择一个已有 DFT 数据基础的体系，按“训练集同时覆盖原子位移和自旋构型，显式标注交换、各向异性、DMI 或自旋力；用自旋 MD/MC 与 DFT 自旋能差验证温度、应变和缺陷下的磁序稳定性”补充训练/验证集，再比较《High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys》对应模型对相稳定、极化/磁序、缺陷或动力学指标的改进。若结果只在训练分布内有效，应通过跨温度、跨应变、跨缺陷浓度和跨超胞测试检查可迁移性。第一步可以选取团队已有的 HfO₂、二维磁体、半导体缺陷或钙钛矿数据做小样本试验，再决定是否扩大到生产级计算。

core_items.title_en: Checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice states in overdoped cuprate superconductors
core_items.title_zh: 文献研究：Checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice states in overdoped cuprate superconductors
core_items.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77985-0 In cuprate superconductors, the overdoped regime has received comparatively limited attention. Here, broadband optical spectroscopy and DQMC calculations reveal an electronic reconstruction in LSCO beyond x > 0.2, consistent with a checkerboard Zhang–Rice configuration hosting coexisting localized and itinerant carriers.
